sections.title: How I prepare
paragraphs: I do not try to learn every tool from a job description. I refresh the stack I actually used: Playwright, API, SQL, CI, and how I explain the QA process.
I keep two versions of answers. Ukrainian is how I think. English is spoken: short sentences, one idea each, with real technical words (fixtures, storageState, 401).
I practice the story of the work, not only tool names: first QA on a project, what I automated and why, how I look for a root cause.

sections.title: What I am learning now
paragraphs: Interview prep around Playwright: fixtures, storageState, APIRequest, locators that stay stable, why a test is flaky.
How to explain a framework and Jenkins jobs (merge request, branch, nightly) in a clear way.
Spoken English for work answers. My level is Intermediate / B1. I say that honestly.
SQL and API checks for defect investigation — QA-level, not DBA or performance specialist work.

sections.title: Playwright — short conspect
paragraphs: This is my main automation stack now: TypeScript and Playwright. I use it for UI, API (APIRequest), and end-to-end flows.
Framework shape I use: OOP, page objects, fixtures. Login is not repeated in every test when storageState can hold the session (cookies / auth).
I look at locators, frames, parallel runs, and flaky tests as part of the job, not as a surprise at the end.
I also used Java, Selenium, and Maven in commercial work at RIA.com. At Clear Junction and FRACTAL I used TypeScript and Playwright. Playwright is what I use today.

sections.title: What I automate — and what I do not
paragraphs: I automate flows that run often and must stay green in CI: regression, critical UI + API paths, repeated setup.
I do not automate everything. A test that is weak, tied to a random UI, or expensive to keep is worse than a short manual check.
A useful automated test is one the team can trust after a merge, not a screenshot of a click path that breaks every sprint.

sections.title: How I use Cursor
paragraphs: I use Cursor every day. I read generated code. I do not merge it blindly.
AI helps with boilerplate and first drafts. I still own locators, waits, test data, and whether the assertion matches the real risk.
